records.label: Tongatapu, Tonga: observed locally supported population floor
pressure_evidence: Green's Tongatapu reconstruction gives a late-prehistoric/contact-era population floor of approximately 15,000–17,000 and an upper envelope of 18,000–24,000.
Archaeobotanical evidence documents near-complete primary-forest removal, intensive multi-cropping, bush-fallow pressure, and expansion after local intensification limits.
The boundary is the whole Tongatapu island; the food regime is locally produced yam, taro, sweet potato, banana, breadfruit, coconut, fishing, and livestock.
records.boundary_description: Entire Tongatapu island, Kingdom of Tonga
records.boundary_source: Ussher 2015 archaeobotanical dissertation, summarising Green 1973, Kirch 1984/1988 and Burley 2007
records.source_family_independence: archaeobotany_and_historical_population_reconstruction; capacity upper envelope is not used as a two-sided target
records.notes: This is a one-sided floor only: capacity_low is set to the independently documented locally supported population floor, while central/high are placeholders ignored by lower-bound likelihoods. It does not promote Green's model-derived upper envelope to a scale target. The EU5 crosswalk applies the cited GSHHG land fraction to the coarse Tongatapu footprint: 253.86 km2 versus approximately 260 km2 historical island area (97.64% coverage).
